<TEI xmlns='http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0'><seg xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" type="excerpt" xml:id="ex61032023-09-26-091118" status="unreviewed">
               <milestone n="Lineage 1" unit="section"/>
               'di'i rgyud pa lugs ka la | 
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3829">pu to ba</rs> yan blo sbyong chen po dang ka|gcig?| </l>
               <l>de nas <rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4104">glang thang ba<!--Glang ri thang pa rdo rje seng+ge P3445 1054-1123--></rs> × </l>
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4156">dgyal pa chos 'bar<!--Sha mi sgom chen Smon lam 'bar? This was a student of Glang thang pa but the only syllable in common with the name given in the colophon is the final 'bar. The more likely person at this point of the transmission lineage would be Sha ra ba Yon tan grags but the name doesn't match.--></rs> ×</l>
                
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3874">'chad kha ba</rs> <note>ye shes rdo rje</note> </l>
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3859">se spyil phu ba <note type="gloss">chos kyi rgyal mtshan</note></rs> × </l> 
            <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:6910">lha chen po <!--Lha chen lung gi dbang phyug--></rs></l>
                <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4048">lha 'gro mgon <!--Lha 'gro ba'i mgon po--></rs> </l>
           <anchor xml:id="a7"/>× 
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3977">mchims <expan>nam mkha'</expan> grags</rs>| </l>
<!--'Chad kha ba Ye shes rdo rje P3447, the teacher of Se spyil phu|pu ba Chos kyi rgyal mtshan P3448 (next in the list), who in turn was the teacher of Lha chen lung gi dbang phyug P3449 (next in the list), who in turn was the teacher of Lha 'gro ba'i mgon po P4137 (next in the list). It then follows the author Mchims Nam mkha' grags-->

<milestone n="Lineage 2" unit="section"/>
<note type="editorial"/><!--Zhang ston Chos kyi bla ma? 1184- 1241 but if this is the case it means that this is an alternative lineage that goes again down to Mchims Nam mkha' grags pa. One thing that might indicate that here we are indeed encountering a second lineage is the <mentioned>shad</mentioned> that divides Nam mkha grags' name from the next name. None of the preceding names were separated by <mentioned>shad</mentioned>-s but only sometimes by longer spaces. None of the names that follow after this <mentioned>shad</mentioned> are again separated by <mentioned>shad</mentioned>-s.Then we could read the second transmission lineage as such: “Blo chen ston ZhaNG” = Zhang ston chos kyi bla ma 5th abbot of Snar thang; “Mkhan po Seng rgyal ba” = Sangs rgyas sgom pa Seng ge grags  (P1060) 5th abbot of Snar thang; “Sang 'od pa” = Sangs rgyas sgom pa Seng ge skyabs (P2640) 6th abbot of Snar thang consequently the ‘bdag' could only refer to Mchims Nam mkha' grags himself. This would mean that the person who wrote down this annotation is the author himself.-->
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3890"><!--Tentative identification as "Zhang ston"-->slob dpon ston zhang<anchor xml:id="a8"/></rs> 
               ×</l> 
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:4158">Sang 'od? pa</rs> ×</l> 
               <l><rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:named_reference" ref="db:3976"><!--Tentative identification as Sangs rgyas sgom pa Seng ge skyabs,  1179-1250-->mkhan po seng rgyal ba</rs></l> 
               <l>des <rs type="person" ana="corpusmd:unnamed_reference" ref="db:4593">bdag</rs> so</l></seg></TEI>
